headline: Multi-omic integration nominates candidate genes and loci for complex disease traits
label: Integrative Genetic Target Prioritization
summary: Expanding single-cell, spatial, and plasma proteomic QTL resources now let GWAS loci be resolved to tissue, cell type, and context.
synthesis: The dominant thread is integration of GWAS summary statistics with molecular QTL, protein interaction, or network data to nominate candidate genes and loci. Mendelian randomization and colocalization anchor several studies, including proteome-wide MR that prioritizes ADM and CFH for osteoarthritis and colocalization that reports four druggable loci for hypothermia. Other items resolve associations to tissue or cell type: spatial single-cell atlases map shared psoriasis and metabolic syndrome genetics, and STARNET plasma proteomics in 532 CAD patients links proteins to tissue origins and cross-tissue regulatory networks. Network-based prioritization appears in WGCNA with explainable machine learning for HMOX2 in vascular aging and heart failure, and in MGST3 defining a mitochondrial-health M2 macrophage state in atherosclerosis. What is new is a shift toward context dependence: CASTIE tests genotype-by-context interactions in single-cell eQTL mapping and finds context-dependent regulatory variants. Most items remain prioritization studies, though several add experimental validation such as AP-MS, qPCR, or mouse work.
